enso.rule: CPC official RONI of the winter the lead window covers: strong El Nino if NDJ or DJF >= 1.5, El Nino if >= 0.5, La Nina if NDJ or DJF <= -0.5

na: SEAS5 expects the Pacific ridge regime on 5% of JFM days against 24% in its own climate (less often; members 4–7%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.48, 90% interval 0.26 to 0.66, p 0.002, passes the false-discovery test).

SEAS5 expects the Pacific ridge regime on 6% of DJF days against 24% in its own climate (less often; members 4–8%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.36, 90% interval 0.11 to 0.57, p 0.017, passes the false-discovery test).

SEAS5 expects the Pacific trough regime on 38% of JFM days against 26% in its own climate (more often; members 35–42%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.48, 90% interval 0.22 to 0.70, p 0.002, passes the false-discovery test).

SEAS5 expects the Pacific trough regime on 35% of February days against 26% in its own climate (more often; members 31–40%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.51, 90% interval 0.24 to 0.72, p 0.002, passes the false-discovery test).
In the hindcast's 14 El Niño winters the Pacific trough regime was observed +8 points in DJF (significant), and SEAS5 predicted +5 — same sign, also significant.
In the hindcast's 14 El Niño winters the Pacific ridge regime was observed -9 points in JFM (significant), and SEAS5 predicted -9 — same sign, also significant.
ea: SEAS5 expects the Atlantic ridge regime on 12% of November days against 20% in its own climate (less often; members 9–16%), and its hindcast has significant skill for that regime there (r 0.38, 90% interval 0.17 to 0.58, p 0.012, passes the false-discovery test).

Where the hindcast is skilful its shifts are too small for that skill: median ratio of predictable components 1.7 over those 3 cells (1 = a well-sized signal), so the observed shift is typically larger than the forecast one — read the sign, not the size.
